name: Bridges
rules: Connect the islands with bridges so each island has exactly its number. Bridges run straight, never cross, and at most two join a pair.
technique.1: This island can only reach its number by using every bridge that still fits around it, so draw all of them.
technique.2: This island's number is too big to leave any neighbour out, so it needs at least one bridge in every direction it can reach.
technique.3: Without a bridge to this neighbour, the other directions could not give this island enough bridges for its number, so a bridge must go here.
demo.1: Join the islands with bridges. The number on an island is how many bridges must reach it.
demo.2: Bridges run straight between two islands and never cross. This one counts one at each end.
demo.3: The same pair can take a second bridge. Now it counts two at each end.
demo.4: No island can go over its number. This one needs three bridges and has four.
demo.5: One bridge down the side instead of two, and it has its three.
demo.6: Every number matched, and every island joined to the rest. That finishes it.
hint.allSpaces.plain: The {n} in row {row}, column {column} needs every bridge that still fits around it to reach {n}. So each ? gap that is still open gets as many bridges as it can hold.
hint.allSpaces.fresh: The {n} in row {row}, column {column} needs {n} bridges, and its gaps can take no more than {n} between them. So every ? gap gets as many bridges as it can hold.
hint.allSpaces.closed: Around the {n} in row {row}, column {column}, the gaps not crossed, ruled out or ending at a full island can take no more than {n} bridges between them. So each of those ? gaps gets as many bridges as it can hold.
hint.allSpaces.more: The {n} in row {row}, column {column} still needs {need} bridges, and the gaps around it not yet decided, crossed or ending at a full island can take no more than {need} between them. So each of those ? gaps gets as many bridges as it can hold.
hint.oneEachWay.plain: The {n} in row {row}, column {column} is too big to leave out any neighbour it can still reach: the others could never reach {n}. So every ? gap that is still open needs at least one bridge.
hint.oneEachWay.count: The {n} in row {row}, column {column} can still reach {count} neighbours. Leave any one of them out and the others can take at most {max} bridges, short of {n}. So every ? gap that is still open needs at least one bridge.
hint.needsNeighbour.many: Some gaps around the {n} in row {row}, column {column} can't be left empty: without a bridge in any one of them, the rest could not reach {n}. So each of those ? gaps needs at least one bridge.
hint.needsNeighbour.one: Without a bridge to the {m} in row {mrow}, column {mcolumn}, the other gaps around the {n} in row {row}, column {column} can take at most {max} bridges, short of {n}. So the ? gap between them needs at least one bridge.
hint.needsNeighbour.onePlain: The other gaps around the {n} in row {row}, column {column} can't reach {n} without a bridge to the {m} in row {mrow}, column {mcolumn}. So the ? gap between them needs at least one bridge.
hint.needsNeighbour.two: The other gaps around the {n} in row {row}, column {column} can't reach {n} without a bridge to the {a} in row {arow}, column {acolumn}, nor without one to the {b} in row {brow}, column {bcolumn}. So both of those ? gaps need at least one bridge.
